title: Mapped Optional
description:
Implement two mapped types:
- `MapOptional<T>` — makes all properties optional (like `Partial<T>`)
- `MapRequired<T>` — makes all properties required (like `Required<T>`)

Do not use the built-in utility types.

**Example:**
```ts
type O = MapOptional<{ a: number; b: string }>; // { a?: number; b?: string }
type R = MapRequired<{ a?: number; b?: string }>; // { a: number; b: string }
```
starter_code:
export type MapOptional<T> = // your type here

export type MapRequired<T> = // your type here
solution:
export type MapOptional<T> = { [K in keyof T]?: T[K] };

export type MapRequired<T> = { [K in keyof T]-?: T[K] };
ai_context: Common mistake: confusing `?` (add optional) with `-?` (remove optional). The `-` modifier prefix is a mapped type modifier that explicitly strips the optional flag.
